profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne cluster sits in the Cincinnati metro area, spanning Cincinnati, Lebanon, and Butler and Warren Counties in Ohio and Florence, Kentucky just across the Ohio River. This is CyrusOne home market: Wikipedia coverage states Cincinnati Bell purchased CyrusOne for 525 million dollars in 2010 and later divested its remaining stake in 2015 after the company IPO in 2013. CyrusOne was originally founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten. The company was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Florence publishes 5 MW of IT capacity in northern Kentucky, making it the largest disclosed data center in the state by a significant margin at 52 percent of Kentucky's three reporting facilities.

The facility holds compliance certifications for regulated workloads: PCI DSS for payment card processing, HIPAA for healthcare, FISMA for government, plus ISO 27001 and SSAE 16 Type II. This certification profile indicates the site targets enterprise and regulated-industry tenants rather than hyperscale AI operations. Hyperscale AI training clusters do not depend on these compliance certifications and typically pursue different infrastructure strategies.

The 5 MW capacity could theoretically host roughly 500 accelerators in a dense AI training configuration, though CyrusOne does not specify the actual workload mix. The 143,000 square feet of technical space is published. Kentucky's three reporting facilities total 9.55 MW, placing the state well outside the binding constraints on US AI infrastructure growth. The operator does not disclose full campus capacity or individual facility power allocations.
